Question: According to KOC.SA.002, how often must an in-service scaffold be re-inspected by an authorized Scaffolding Inspector, whether or not it has been used?
D: Only after alterations or bad weather
Reference: Cl. 4.1.3 / 5.1.6: inspection before first use, after alteration, after adverse weather and every 7 days thereafter.

Question: Above what wind speed does KOC.SA.002 prohibit work on or from scaffolds?
D: 80 km/h
Reference: Cl. 5.1.3 c): work on scaffolds is prohibited during storms or high winds (wind speed more than 65 km/h).

Question: An elevated scaffold work area requires at least two means of exit when the horizontal travel distance to the nearest exit ladder exceeds:
Reference: Cl. 5.1.3 f): where horizontal travel distance to the nearest exit exceeds 15 m (50 ft), at least two means of exit are required.

Question: A worker is setting up a portable ladder against a structure. Which set-up ratio meets the KOC.SA.002 requirement of approximately 76 degrees?
A: 1 m out for every 2 m up
B: 1 m out for every 3 m up
C: 1 m out for every 4 m up
D: 1 m out for every 6 m up
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2 h): ladders shall be set at an angle of 76 degrees (1 m out for 4 m up).

Question: Where no adequate handhold is provided at the landing, a portable ladder must extend above the landing place by at least:
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2 i): the ladder must rise at least 1.05 m (3.5 ft) above the landing place.

Question: Without a supporting risk assessment, what is the minimum distance a scaffold may be erected from an existing excavation?
D: 3 m
Reference: Cl. 5.1.3 aa): no scaffold shall be erected less than 3 m from an existing excavation; a shorter distance only based on a risk assessment.

Question: What minimum experience does KOC.SA.002 require for a Scaffolding Supervisor, in addition to certified erection and dismantling training?
A: 3 years in scaffolding, with no supervisory requirement
B: 5 years in scaffolding, including at least 1 year as a supervisor
C: 5 years in scaffolding, including at least 3 years as a supervisor
D: 10 years in scaffolding, including at least 2 years as a supervisor
Reference: Cl. 5.1.2 b): minimum 5 years' experience in scaffolding jobs, of which at least one year in a supervisory role.

Question: What is the maximum permitted height of a portable stepladder under KOC.SA.002?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.3 f): portable stepladders shall not exceed 20 ft (6.1 m) in height.

Question: What is the maximum validity of a Hot, Cold or Radiography Work Permit from its date of issue, subject to renewal by the Permit Issuer?
D: 14 consecutive days
Reference: Cl. 5.4: Hot / Cold / Radiography permits are valid for a maximum of seven consecutive days from the date of issue, subject to renewal.

Question: A Work Permit endorsement or renewal remains valid for a maximum of:
D: The full permit validity period
Reference: Cl. 5.8 e): each endorsement / renewal is valid for a maximum of one shift (12 hours) or as recorded by the Permit Issuer.

Question: A worksite was gas tested and certified gas free at 07:00, but the job could not start until 09:30. What must happen before work starts?
A: Work may start because the certificate is valid for the shift
B: Work may start if the Worksite Supervisor signs the permit
C: A new gas test must be carried out
D: Work may start if a fire watch is posted
Reference: Cl. 5.15 b): if work has not started within 2 hours of a gas test, the gas free certification becomes invalid and a new test is required.

Question: What is the maximum flammable gas reading permitted for authorizing Hot Work under the KOC Permit to Work Procedure?
D: 20% LEL
Reference: Cl. 5.13.2 / 5.15 g): the maximum LEL permissible for authorized Hot Work is 0% LEL.

Question: During cold work on a flowline, 0% LEL cannot be achieved despite depressurizing, venting and purging. Under what condition may the work proceed?
A: Below 10% LEL, continuously monitored, with an approved Method Statement
B: Below 20% LEL, with all workers wearing breathing apparatus sets
C: Below 25% LEL, with a fire watch and extinguishers posted at site
D: Any LEL reading, with verbal approval from the Permit Issuer
Reference: Cl. 5.13.1 c): work may be carried out ensuring LEL does not exceed 10% under continuous monitoring; a reviewed and approved Method Statement is mandatory.

Question: What is the maximum period a Work Permit can remain suspended before it must be cancelled and signed off?
A: 24 hours, after which it is cancelled
B: 3 days, after which it is cancelled
C: 5 days, or permit expiry if sooner
D: 7 days, regardless of permit expiry
Reference: Cl. 5.11: a Work Permit can be suspended for a maximum of 5 days or until expiry of its validity, whichever is sooner.

Question: What is the minimum fire extinguisher provision for each Hot Work location under KOC.SA.004?
D: Three extinguishers within 10 m
Reference: Cl. 5.16 a): a minimum of two fire extinguishers (9 kg Monnex or 12 kg DCP) within 7.5 m of each hot work location.

Question: Unless otherwise stated in the permit, how long is an Excavation Notification valid from the date the Asset Owner signs it?
D: 90 days
Reference: Cl. 5.13.6 e): the Excavation Notification is valid for 90 days from the date of issuance.

Question: What is the minimum passing score for the PTW qualifying written test for Permit Issuers, Permit Applicants and Worksite Supervisors?
Reference: Cl. 5.7 b): the passing score for the PTW qualifying test shall be a minimum of 70%.

Question: Under KOC.SA.004, mechanical excavation is NOT allowed within what radius of any underground facility?
D: 5 m
Reference: Cl. 5.13.6 a): mechanical excavation is not allowed inside the plant or facility or within 5 m radius of any underground facilities.

Question: During a routine check, an SCBA breathing air cylinder gauge shows it has dropped below full charge. At what point does KOC.SA.005 require it to be sent for recharging?
A: When pressure falls to 90% of the specified pressure
B: When pressure falls to 75% of the specified pressure
C: When pressure falls to 50% of the specified pressure
D: When the low-pressure alarm sounds
Reference: Cl. 4.2 / 5.4.3: cylinder pressure must not be less than 90% of full capacity; refill when pressure drops to 90% of specified pressure.

Question: When checking an SCBA, the cylinder valve is closed slowly to test the low-pressure warning alarm. At approximately what level of cylinder capacity should the alarm sound?
Reference: Cl. 5.4.5 C: verify activation of the low pressure alarm (to sound at approximately 25% of cylinder capacity).

Question: What is the maximum validity of an RPE 'Authorized User Card' issued by the Controlling Team?
D: 36 months
Reference: Cl. 5.4.4: validity of the Authorized User Card shall not exceed 12 months and must be within the medical examination validity.

Question: What periodic hydrostatic test intervals does KOC.SA.005 specify for SCBA breathing air cylinders?
A: Steel every 3 years; composite every 5 years
B: Steel every 5 years; composite every 3 years
C: Steel and composite both every 5 years
D: Steel and composite both every 10 years
Reference: Cl. 5.4.5 C: verify SCBA cylinder is current on hydrostatic test (5 years for steel, 3 years for composite cylinders).

Question: A worker passes a quantitative fit test with a full-face respirator. Which requirement then applies on the job?
A: Any model from the same manufacturer may be used
B: Any size of the same model may be used
C: The exact same make, model, style and size must be used
D: Any tight-fitting respirator with the same APF may be used
Reference: Cl. 5.7: after passing a fit test, the user must use the exact same make, model, style and size of respirator; fit testing is at least annual.

Question: What minimum specification does KOC.SA.005 set for SCBA used by emergency services (Fire Group)?
A: Negative pressure type, minimum 30 minutes duration
B: Positive pressure type, minimum 30 minutes duration
C: Positive pressure type, minimum 45 minutes duration
D: Positive pressure type, minimum 60 minutes duration
Reference: Cl. 5.2.1 Note 1: SCBA for emergency services shall be positive pressure type with minimum 45 minutes duration, conforming to NFPA 1981.

Question: An air-purifying respirator filter has been removed from its sealed packaging but rarely used. When must it be replaced, regardless of use?
D: After 12 months
Reference: Cl. 5.4.5 B: a filter once opened from the seal must be replaced after 6 months regardless of its use.

Question: How often, at a minimum, must the output air quality of a breathing air compressor be checked?
A: Every month, and after each filter change
B: Every 3 months, and after each filter change
C: Every 6 months, and after each filter change
D: Every 12 months, and after each filter change
Reference: Cl. 5.9: periodic checks of compressor output air quality at least once every 3 months and after each filter change.

Question: Which set of gas test results permits confined space entry WITHOUT respiratory protection under KOC.SA.007 Table 1?
D: O2 16–21%, flammables < 10% LEL, H2S < 100 ppm
Reference: Table 1: entry without respiratory protection when O2 is 19.5–23.5%, flammables < 10% LEL and H2S < 10 ppm.

Question: Gas testing of a vessel shows 15% oxygen. According to KOC.SA.007 Table 1, what is the correct action?
A: Entry permitted with an air-purifying respirator
B: Entry permitted with forced ventilation only
C: Entry permitted with SCBA and continuous monitoring
D: No entry, except in an emergency or for rescue
Reference: Table 1: oxygen content less than 16% (or H2S > 100 ppm, or flammables 50% LEL or above) = NO ENTRY except emergency or rescue.

Question: The initial confined space gas test was done at 08:00 but entry is delayed until 09:15. What does KOC.SA.007 require?
A: Entry may proceed because the test is valid for the shift
B: A follow-up gas test by the Worksite Supervisor before entry
C: A new Confined Space Entry Certificate must be raised
D: Entry may proceed if entrants wear personal H2S monitors
Reference: Cl. 5.3: entry is to take place within one hour of the initial gas test; otherwise a follow-up gas test by the Worksite Supervisor is required before entry.

Question: Where periodic (rather than continuous) gas monitoring is used during a confined space entry, the interval between tests shall not exceed:
D: 4 hours
Reference: Cl. 5.13: the periodic monitoring of gas shall not exceed a two-hour period.

Question: How frequently does KOC.SA.007 require personnel working inside a vessel or tank to be given a rest period, unless conditions require more frequent breaks?
D: Every 2 hours
Reference: Cl. 5.11: personnel working inside the vessel / tank will be given a rest period at each 30 minute interval, or more frequently.

Question: Inside a KOC hydrocarbon facility, an excavation is classified as a confined space when its depth exceeds:
Reference: Cl. 2.0 c): excavation with depth more than 1.2 m inside hydrocarbon facilities is a confined space.

Question: An entrant collapses inside a vessel. What is the correct immediate action for the standby person who is not trained in search and rescue?
A: Enter at once wearing an escape set and pull the entrant out
B: Summon aid via the Control Room and stay outside until relief arrives
C: Send another entrant inside to assist the casualty to the manway
D: Lower a spare SCBA set to the casualty and wait at the manway
Reference: Cl. 4.4 Note / 5.11: the standby person must not enter until relief arrives; he must summon aid immediately via the Control Room.

Question: Which of the following must NEVER be used to ventilate a confined space?
D: An air-driven extraction fan
Reference: Cl. 5.5: compressed oxygen or instrument air shall never be used to ventilate a confined space.

Question: A vessel has been certified gas free but flammable residues may remain. If extra-low-voltage portable lighting is used, what is its maximum voltage under KOC.SA.007?
D: 240 V AC
Reference: Cl. 5.6: such spaces may be illuminated by extra low voltage (25 V AC) portable lighting approved for Zone 1; transformers never taken inside.

Question: On a bench-mounted grinder, what is the maximum gap permitted between the work rest and the abrasive wheel?
D: 1 inch
Reference: Cl. 5.1.2.1: work rest adjusted as close to the wheel as possible at a maximum distance of 1/4 inch.

Question: The 'ring test' described in KOC.SA.012 for checking an abrasive wheel for cracks is applicable to which type of wheel?
B: Small wheels of 100 mm diameter or less
D: Plate-mounted and segment wheels
Reference: Cl. 5.1.2.3 / 5.1.2.5: the ring test is used only for vitrified bonded wheels; it is not practicable for small, mounted, segment or plate-mounted wheels.

Question: After a new abrasive wheel is mounted, how long should it be allowed to run free, with users standing clear, before use?
D: About 5 minutes
Reference: Cl. 5.1.2.3: new wheels should be allowed to run free for about 60 seconds; users should stand clear.

Question: A technician is selecting a cutting disc for a portable grinder. Which speed rating requirement must the disc meet?
A: Rated at or above the RPM of the grinder
B: Rated at 75% of the grinder RPM
C: Rated below the grinder RPM to reduce vibration
D: Any rating, provided a speed governor is fitted
Reference: Cl. 5.1.2.1: ensure speed of the wheel is compatible with the machine, i.e. use a wheel or disc rated at or above the RPM of the grinder.

Question: Under KOC.SA.012, a mobile air compressor may be deployed in a Zone 2 hazardous area only:
A: Under a Cold Work Permit with continuous gas monitoring
B: Under a Hot Work Permit, if suitable for the area classification
C: Under a Vehicle Entry Permit, if a spark arrestor is fitted
D: It is never permitted in a Zone 2 area
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2: mobile compressors are not permitted in Zone 0 & 1; in Zone 2 they must be covered by an authorized Hot Work Permit, subject to suitability.

Question: Which method of connecting a pneumatic tool to its high-pressure air hose is acceptable under KOC.SA.012?
A: Screw-adjusted 'Jubilee' clip, tightened with a screwdriver
B: Crowfoot coupling with retaining pin/clip and whip check
C: Wire-twisted joint secured with heavy-duty insulation tape
D: Push-fit coupling, with the hose tied to the tool handle
Reference: Cl. 5.2.1 / 5.2.3: purpose-made connections (e.g. crowfoot) with retaining pin/clip and whip; 'Jubilee' type connections are not permitted.

Question: At or above what noise level from air compressors and pneumatic tools must warning signs be displayed and hearing protection worn?
D: 90 dB
Reference: Cl. 5.2.1: if noise levels are at or above 85 dB, signs must be displayed and hearing protection worn.

Question: Abrasive wheels in a store have been in stock for more than two years. What does KOC.SA.012 recommend before they are issued?
A: Issue them only for light grinding work
B: Consult the manufacturer or supplier first
C: Ring test them all, including resin wheels
D: Discard them without any further assessment
Reference: Cl. 5.1.2.7: in case of doubt, or if wheels have been in stock for more than two years, the manufacturer/supplier should be consulted.

Question: What is the maximum age of a contractor's mobile equipment or heavy vehicle permitted for work in KOC business under KOC.SA.013?
D: 25 years
Reference: Cl. 5.2: contractor mobile equipment / heavy vehicles shall not be older than 20 years, subject to suitability and 3rd party certification.

Question: How often must a contractor's mobile crane (load handling equipment) be inspected and certified by a KOC-approved inspection contractor?
C: Every 12 months or contract duration, whichever is earlier
D: Every 24 months
Reference: Cl. 5.4 I a): general mobile equipment once a year (or contract duration if earlier); load or material handling equipment once every 6 months per KOC.SA.029.

Question: A contractor's forklift is involved in a minor incident and then repaired. What does KOC.SA.013 require before it is used again?
A: The operator completes a pre-use checklist
B: A new Clearance Certificate based on a new inspection report
C: The existing Clearance Certificate is endorsed by the Area HSE Team
D: No action is needed for a minor incident
Reference: Cl. 4.6: after any incident or major repair / modification, a new Clearance Certificate is issued based on a new inspection report from a KOC-approved inspection contractor.

Question: Under KOC.SA.013, gasoline-operated equipment such as a jumping compactor is restricted on site unless it is fitted with:
A: A reverse alarm and a reverse camera
B: Vibration-resistant fuel caps and spark arrestors
D: A dead-man switch and emergency stop button
Reference: Cl. 4.6: gasoline-operated equipment is restricted unless fitted with vibration-resistant fuel caps and spark arrestors.

Question: In which areas does KOC.SA.013 require mobile equipment to hold a valid Clearance Certificate?
A: Only in Zone 0 and Zone 1 hazardous areas
B: Only in hazardous areas inside plant fences
C: In both hazardous and non-hazardous areas
D: Only for equipment with a State registration plate
Reference: Cl. 5.1: all mobile equipment shall require a Clearance Certificate for both hazardous and non-hazardous areas including Ahmadi area.

Question: A contractor wants to move a generator from Contract A to Contract B, both under the same contractor, using Contract A's Clearance Certificate and Gate Pass. Under KOC.SA.013 this is:
A: Acceptable, since the contractor is the same
B: Acceptable, if the certificate is still valid
C: Not acceptable; it must be issued under Contract B
D: Acceptable, with Security Team approval
Reference: Cl. 4.6: contractor cannot use mobile equipment with another contract's Clearance Certificate and Gate Pass, even if the contractor is the same (drilling teams excepted).

Question: During maintenance on a dump truck with a raised bed, which control does KOC.SA.013 require to protect personnel?
A: Lowering the bed onto stacked timber blocks
B: Fitting a mechanical locking device to the raised bed
C: Keeping the engine running so hydraulics hold the bed
D: Posting a banksman to watch the bed during work
Reference: Cl. 5.1.1 (2): no personnel under a raised bed; use appropriate mechanical locking devices during maintenance to prevent sudden bed movement.

Question: Which precaution must be met before a heavy vehicle without an inbuilt spark arrestor is deployed at a KOC worksite?
A: Its exhaust tail pipe must be fitted with a spark arrestor
B: It must be parked at least 30 m from process equipment
C: Its engine must be switched off every 30 minutes
D: Its fuel tank must be at least half full
Reference: Cl. 5.1.1: the exhaust tail pipe is fitted with a spark arrestor in case it is not inbuilt.

Question: In-service flange bolting replacement (hot bolting) is NOT permitted on flanges having fewer than how many bolts?
D: Twelve
Reference: Cl. 5.3: in-service bolt replacement / rework is not permitted on flanges with less than six bolts.

Question: Above what line pressure does KOC.SA.015 prohibit in-service flange bolting replacement?
D: 20.7 bar (300 psi)
Reference: Cl. 5.3: not permitted on high-pressure lines > 13.6 bar (200 psi) including air, nitrogen and hydrocarbons.

Question: A gas line contains 800 ppm of H2S. Under KOC.SA.015, can in-service hot bolting be carried out on it?
A: Yes, if all workers wear SCBA
B: Yes, if line pressure is first reduced
C: No, it is in highly sour service
D: No, any line above 10 ppm is excluded
Reference: Cl. 2.0 / 5.3: highly sour service is > 500 ppm H2S; hot bolting is not permitted on systems in highly sour service.

Question: During in-service bolt replacement on a live flange, how many bolts may be slackened at any one time?
D: Up to one quarter of the bolts
Reference: Cl. 5.3 d): slacken one bolt only; under no circumstances must two bolts be slackened at any one time.

Question: When fitting new bolts during in-service bolt replacement (without tensioning equipment), how far may the bolt protrude beyond the nut?
B: No more than two full threads
C: No more than five full threads
D: At least 25 mm
Reference: Cl. 5.3 h): new bolts should protrude no more than two full threads beyond the nut.

Question: While breaking a flange, the crew finds the bolts are badly corroded and will not turn. What is the only acceptable removal method under KOC.SA.015?
A: Gas cutting with an oxy-acetylene torch
D: Striking the nuts with an iron hammer
Reference: Cl. 5.4: if bolts are corroded, the only acceptable method is a pneumatic hacksaw; gas cutting (open flame) shall not be used.

Question: What is the correct body position and first bolt to loosen when breaking a flange that may still contain pressure?
A: Stand downwind and loosen the bolts nearest to you
B: Stand upwind and loosen the bolts farthest away from you
C: Stand directly in front and loosen bolts clockwise
D: Stand upwind and loosen all bolts evenly at the same time
Reference: Cl. 5.2 o) / 5.5 a): maintain a safe upwind position and loosen bolts farthest away first so any release sprays away from the worker.

Question: Which type of hammer may be used when breaking flanges on lines in hydrocarbon service?
D: Any hammer, if a fire watch is present
Reference: Cl. 5.4: do not use an iron hammer in hydrocarbon service because impact will generate sparks; only brass hammers shall be used.

Question: A leak clamp has been installed on a process line. Within what period does KOC.SA.017 require the original integrity of the line to be restored?
D: 12 months
Reference: Cl. 5.2: all clamps are temporary; appropriate actions shall be taken to restore original integrity within three months.

Question: If permanent repair cannot be done within the initial period, a Clamp Joint Evaluation Meeting may authorize the clamp for a further maximum of:
D: 12 months
Reference: Cl. 5.2 / 5.3: the Asset Owner may request extension through the Clamp Joint Evaluation Meeting for a maximum of six months after the initial three months.

Question: How far in advance must the Asset Owner submit a Clamp Extension Request, with valid justification, before the agreed clamp period expires?
D: At least 30 working days
Reference: Cl. 5.4: request shall be submitted at least ten working days prior to exceeding the agreed period; authorization from Group Manager (Ops/GO).

Question: Inspection finds that the leak on a pipeline is caused by a crack. What does KOC.SA.017 require?
A: Fit a bolt-on mechanical clamp rated for the MAOP
B: Fit a sealing band clamp centred on the crack
C: Do not clamp; replace the cracked spool with new pipe
D: Fit a split sleeve clamp and de-rate the line
Reference: Cl. 5.2: if a crack appears on any area of the piping, clamping shall not be used; the cracked portion shall be replaced with a new pipe spool.

Question: What pressure capability must a bolt-on mechanical leak clamp have under KOC.SA.017?
A: At least 50% of the line's operating pressure
B: At least equal to the normal operating pressure only
C: Capable of containing the MAOP of the carrier pipe
D: Equal to the hydrotest pressure of the clamp only
Reference: Cl. 4.3 / 5.2: clamp design pressure not less than that of the piping; the clamp must be capable of containing the MAOP of the carrier pipe.

Question: When sealing band clamps are used on isolated external corrosion pits, what is the minimum spacing between two such clamps?
A: No two clamps within one pipe diameter of each other
B: No two clamps within 0.5 m of each other
C: No two clamps within three pipe diameters of each other
D: No minimum spacing applies between clamps
Reference: Cl. 5.2: no two such clamps shall be installed within one pipe diameter of each other.

Question: When a pipeline leak occurs at a KOC facility, to whom must it be reported in the first instance under KOC.SA.017?
C: Asset PSM Team within 10 working days
D: Contracts Group through the Clamp Register
Reference: Cl. 5.1: whenever a leak occurs it shall be reported to ERCU at 160 and all concerned per KOC.GE.007.

Question: A pipeline leak is caused by general corrosion and shows signs of multiple leaks. Which repair means should be considered first?
A: A sealing band clamp at each leak point
C: Epoxy wrap over the corroded area
D: A bolt-on clamp on the largest leak only
Reference: Cl. 5.2: clamps are for localized pitting leaks; for general corrosion with multiple leaks, a split sleeve clamp should be considered first.

Question: What minimum horizontal radius of warning barricade does KOC.SA.019 require around a hot-tapping site?
Reference: Cl. 5.3.1 xxii: hot-tapping site shall have a warning barricade with a horizontal radius not less than 15 m; mobile equipment kept upwind outside it.

Question: When a line packer or seal plug is used, how must the end of its vent pipe be arranged?
A: At least 15 m away and left open to atmosphere
B: At least 30 m away and dipped in a water bucket
C: At least 30 m away and connected to the flare
D: At least 50 m away and fitted with an end cap
Reference: Cl. 4.4 / 5.3.3: vent pipe end kept at least 30 m away, dipped in a bucket of clear water, monitored continuously; stop work if bubbles appear.

Question: Under KOC.SA.019, for which activity is the signature of the KOC Inspection Engineer required on the work permit?
D: All hot-tapping, welding and plugging work
Reference: Cl. 4.2: Inspection Engineer approval is required only for in-service welding, after confirming remaining wall thickness.

Question: How should the hot-tapping machine be installed with respect to the operator's position?
A: So the operator stands downwind of the machine
B: So the operator stands upwind of the machine
C: So the operator stands directly above the cutter
D: Wind direction is not a consideration
Reference: Cl. 4.4: ensure the hot-tapping machine is installed in such a way that the operator is positioned in the upwind direction.

Question: How must the weight of the hot-tapping machine be managed during the operation?
A: Rest fully on the pipeline being tapped
B: Be independently supported off the pipeline
C: Be held by a crane throughout the operation
D: Be supported on scaffolding tied to the pipe
Reference: Cl. 5.3.1 xix: the hot-tapping machine shall be independently supported; its weight shall not be transferred to the equipment being tapped.

Question: Which statement about sparking tools is correct under KOC.SA.019?
A: They are prohibited during both hot-tapping and welding
B: They are allowed during hot-tapping but not during welding
C: They are not allowed during hot-tapping but are allowed during welding
D: They are allowed during both if a fire watch is present
Reference: Cl. 5.3.1 xviii: sparking tools shall not be used during hot tapping; however, they are allowed during welding.

Question: During a plugging operation, which step is designated a 'HOLD POINT' to be witnessed by the Company's representative?
D: Completion of the JSA
Reference: Cl. 5.3.3: installation of the gas plug shall be a 'HOLD POINT' witnessed by the Company's representative.

Question: During hot-tapping, a leak develops at the machine flange. What must the Worksite Supervisor ensure first?
A: Retrieve the cutter, close the valve and stop safely
B: Continue cutting at reduced speed to finish the bore
C: Tighten the flange bolts while the machine is running
D: Have the fire watch spray the flange and continue
Reference: Cl. 4.4: if any hazardous situation (e.g. leak) is observed, ensure the cutter is retrieved, the isolation valve closed and hot work stopped safely.

Question: While welding is in progress, within what radius of the work must the assigned Fire Watch remain until relieved?
Reference: Cl. 4.5: the Fire Watch shall remain within 8 m radius of the work vicinity during welding / cutting until relieved.

Question: After a welding job is completed, how long must the Fire Watch remain at the location?
D: At least 60 minutes
Reference: Cl. 4.5: remain at least 30 minutes after hot work until the area is inspected and found free of ignition sources.

Question: Before welding in a plant area, flammable materials must be cleared, and drains covered with wet tarpaulins, within what distance of the worksite?
Reference: Cl. 5.7: flammable materials cleared at least 20 m away; all drains within 20 m covered with wet tarpaulins weighted with sandbags.

Question: Under KOC.SA.021, acetylene must not be generated, piped or used at a pressure exceeding:
D: 50 psig
Reference: Cl. 5.4: under no condition shall acetylene be used at a pressure in excess of 15 psig (103 kPa gauge).

Question: Why must fittings containing more than 70% copper (other than a burner tip) not be used in acetylene welding equipment?
A: Copper corrodes rapidly in contact with oxygen
B: Copper and acetylene form explosive copper acetylide
C: Copper conducts heat back and causes flashback
D: Copper lowers the flame temperature too much
Reference: Cl. 5.2: copper in contact with acetylene is liable to form a dangerous explosive compound, copper acetylide.

Question: Which filter lens shade range does KOC.SA.021 specify for electric arc welding?
Reference: Cl. 5.3 Lens Shade Guide: arc welding 10–14; torch brazing 3–4; gas welding 4–8; cutting 3–6.

Question: What minimum distance must an electric arc welding generator be kept from the hot work area?
Reference: Cl. 5.5: the welding generator should be kept at least 5 m away from the hot work area.

Question: A pipe must be cold cut inside a hazardous area. Which equipment is permitted under KOC.SA.021?
B: Pneumatic cold cutting machine or manual cutter
C: Abrasive disc cutter with a spark guard
D: Any cutter, provided a fire watch is present
Reference: Cl. 5.6: in a hazardous area only pneumatic cold cutting machines and manual cutters are allowed; electric-driven cutting machines are not allowed.

Question: Under the KOC multi-lock sequence for electrical isolation, who applies the FIRST lock?
A: The Permit Issuer, before issuing the permit
B: The Authorized Electrical Person, after confirming isolation
C: The Worksite Supervisor, after receiving the permit
D: The Shift Controller, after approving the request
Reference: Cl. 5.6 (i): the first lock shall be applied by the Authorized Electrical Person immediately after confirming electrical isolation.

Question: On completion of work, what is the correct order for removing locks from the multi-lock device before electrical de-isolation?
A: Electrical Person, then Permit Issuer, then Worksite Supervisor
B: Permit Issuer, then Worksite Supervisor, then Electrical Person
C: Worksite Supervisor, then Permit Issuer, then Electrical Person
D: Shift Controller removes all locks together at one time
Reference: Cl. 5.6: the sequence is reversed for removal — Worksite Supervisor / Permit Applicant first, Permit Issuer second, Authorized Electrical Person last.

Question: Which of the following is NOT considered an energy isolating device under KOC.SA.022?
D: A cut-out fuse on the supply circuit
Reference: Cl. 2.0: push buttons, selector switches and other control circuit type devices are not energy isolating devices.

Question: Why does KOC.SA.022 state that Miniature Circuit Breakers (MCBs) should not be used as the point of disconnection?
A: They trip too easily under normal load
B: Positive contact separation cannot be confirmed
C: They cannot be fitted with any warning tag
D: They are only rated for very low voltages
Reference: Cl. 5.1 f): do not use MCBs as disconnections because confirming positive contact separation is generally not possible.

Question: For multi-disciplinary jobs, KOC.SA.022 recommends colour-coded padlocks. Which colour is assigned to Operations?
D: Red
Reference: Cl. 5.6: Yellow – Electrical / Blue – Operation / Black – Mechanical / Red – Instrument.

Question: What is the minimum number of individually marked key storage boxes each facility must have for multi-lockout keys?
Reference: Cl. 5.7: each facility shall have at least 4 key storage boxes (Electrical, Mechanical, Instrumentation & Operation).

Question: An urgent electrical isolation is needed to protect the plant and workforce. Under KOC.SA.022, how may it be authorized?
A: Verbally by the Authorized Electrical Person or Shift Controller
B: Only after a written Electrical Isolation Certificate is approved
C: Verbally by any Worksite Supervisor who is present at site
D: Only by the Asset HSE Team after carrying out a site visit
Reference: Cl. 5.4: emergency isolation can be carried out immediately by verbal approval of the Authorized Electrical Person or Shift Controller; written formalities completed once the emergency is over.

Question: After isolating and locking an electrical motor, how must the absence of voltage be confirmed before work starts?
A: By pressing the local start button to check it does not run
B: By testing with an appropriate and tested voltage tester
C: By checking the breaker indicator light is off
D: By confirming with the Control Room Operator by radio
Reference: Cl. 4.4 / 5.1 j)–k): verify isolation by electrical measurement; presence of voltage must be tested using an appropriate and tested voltage tester.

Question: According to the KOC.SA.024 JSA flow, who initiates, reviews and authorizes a JSA, respectively?
A: Permit Applicant, Permit Issuer, HSE Team
B: Worksite Supervisor, Permit Applicant, Permit Issuer
C: Safety Officer, Worksite Supervisor, Permit Applicant
D: Permit Issuer, Permit Applicant, Worksite Supervisor
Reference: Cl. 5.9 / Appendix 1: JSA initiated by Worksite Supervisor, reviewed by Permit Applicant, authorized by Permit Issuer.

Question: For which activities does KOC.SA.024 require a JSA WITH Task Risk Assessment (initial and residual risk)?
D: Only activities in confined spaces
Reference: Cl. 2.0 / 5.4: JSA with Task Risk Assessment will be carried out only for critical activities.

Question: A contractor submits a JSA copied from a similar job at another gathering centre. Under the 2025 revision of KOC.SA.024, this is:
A: Acceptable if the Permit Issuer signs it
C: Prohibited; a task-specific JSA is needed
D: Acceptable if reviewed at the toolbox talk
Reference: Cl. 5.1 Note: the use of generic JSA is strictly prohibited; a standalone JSA specific to the exact task, location and worksite conditions must be developed.

Question: In KOC.SA.024, 'residual risk' is best defined as the risk:
A: Present before any controls are applied
B: Remaining after controls have been applied
C: Linked to the worst credible outcome only
D: Accepted by the Permit Issuer without controls
Reference: Cl. 2.0: residual risk is the risk remaining after controls have been applied to associated hazards that have been identified.

Question: What size of Risk Assessment Matrix (Severity vs Likelihood) is used in the current KOC JSA template?
Reference: Revision 3 Aug 2025 / Appendix 1: RAM changed to 6x6 Severity vs Likelihood to align with KOC.GE.018.

Question: When a JSA is prepared for a job that involves the use of chemicals, what should it include?
A: A review of the Safety Data Sheets (SDS)
D: A medical surveillance record for each worker
Reference: Cl. 5.5: JSAs for jobs that involve the use of chemicals should include a review of SDS sheets.

Question: On completion of a job carried out under a work permit, where is the JSA sheet retained as a record?
B: With the Permit Issuer, in file
D: It is discarded once the permit is closed
Reference: Cl. 5.7: on completion, the JSA sheet shall be retained in file with the Permit Issuer (routine work without permit: with the Controlling Team).

Question: A Task Risk Assessment shows the residual risk remains in the intolerable region and engineering alternatives are not feasible. Under the KOC JSA risk regime, the activity may proceed only:
A: With Manager-level endorsement and a risk-reduction action plan
B: If the Worksite Supervisor holds an extra toolbox talk on it
C: If the Permit Issuer marks the permit as a critical activity
D: If additional PPE is issued to every worker on the task
Reference: Appendix 1 Risk Control Regime: intolerable risk — activity shall only proceed upon KOC Management endorsement (Manager and above) supported by a detailed action plan.

Question: During excavation in an EOD-certified area, a worker uncovers a suspected unexploded shell. What is the correct sequence of first actions?
A: Lift it out carefully and carry it away from the trench
B: Leave it untouched, clear and mark the area, move away, call 160
C: Photograph it close up on a mobile phone and send it to HSE
D: Cover it with sand and carry on in another part of the trench
Reference: Cl. 5.2.4: do not touch; stop work and clear area; mark location at a safe distance; move away before using radio/phone; inform Fire Station / 160; request EOD assistance.

Question: Before electric shot firing with electric detonators, all radio communication equipment within what range must be switched off?
Reference: Cl. 5.1.3.3: handheld radios / transmitters not within 150 m; all radio equipment within 150 m switched off before electric shot firing.

Question: A charge fired by safety fuse has misfired. What is the minimum time before anyone may approach it?
D: 30 minutes
Reference: Cl. 5.1.3.2: no one should approach until not less than 30 minutes (safety fuse) or 10 minutes (electric firing) has elapsed.

Question: Under KOC.SA.025, no naked flame, spark or source of ignition is permitted within what distance of an explosive storage facility?
Reference: Cl. 5.1.1.2: any naked flame, spark or source of ignition shall not be permitted within 25 m (80 ft) of the explosive storage facility.

Question: As a minimum, how far must a permanent explosive storage facility be located from any other building or place visited by employees or the public?
Reference: Cl. 5.1.1.1: permanent explosive storage must be at least 100 m from any other building, habitation or place liable to be visited.

Question: Which arrangement for transporting explosives and detonators to a well site complies with KOC.SA.025?
A: Both in the same vehicle, in separate compartments
B: Both in the same container, if detonators are shunted
C: In separate vehicles, with no explosives in the driver's cab
D: Detonators in the driver's cab, explosives in the cargo bed
Reference: Cl. 5.1.2: explosives and detonators must be transported separately and not in the same vehicle; no explosive in the driver's cab.

Question: What is the maximum number of charges that should be prepared and loaded for any single firing operation?
D: Twenty
Reference: Cl. 5.1.3.1: a maximum of ten charges should be prepared and loaded for any single firing operation; count the shots fired.

Question: A Controlling Team wants to start work in a new desert area. Which form of EOD clearance is acceptable under KOC.SA.025?
A: Verbal confirmation from the EOD contractor's supervisor
B: A printed EOD certificate with the cleared area marked on a map
C: An e-mail from any HSE Officer stating the area is clear
D: A note on the Permit to Work that the area appears clear
Reference: Cl. 5.2.3: EOD certification shall be issued on printed format with extent of clearance marked on a map; verbal clearance is not acceptable.

Question: What is the minimum distance from a hydrocarbon-carrying pipeline within which mechanical excavation (including levelling with an excavator) is prohibited?
D: 5 m
Reference: Cl. 5.4 b): no mechanical excavation closer than 5 m to any hydrocarbon carrying pipeline, even for levelling.

Question: Without a Management of Change and risk assessment, mechanical excavation should not take place closer than what distance to non-hydrocarbon pipelines, cables and services?
D: 5 m
Reference: Cl. 5.4 c): no mechanical excavation closer than 3 m to non-hydrocarbon pipelines, cables and services; MOC and risk assessment if closer.

Question: In a trench deeper than 1 m, how must access ladders be provided under KOC.SA.026?
A: Projecting 0.5 m above the edge, every 15 m of travel
B: Projecting 1 m above the edge, every 7.5 m of lateral travel
C: Projecting 1 m above the edge, every 15 m of lateral travel
D: Projecting 1.5 m above the edge, at each end only
Reference: Cl. 5.4 i): ladder projecting minimum 1 m above the edge; ladders every 7.5 m (25 ft) of lateral travel, secured top and bottom.

Question: For an excavation up to 1.2 m deep, what is the minimum distance excavated material (spoil) must be placed from the edge?
D: 3 m
Reference: Cl. 5.4 l): excavated material shall be placed not less than 1 m from the edge for depth up to 1.2 m, increased in proportion to depth.

Question: Heavy equipment, materials and excavating machinery must be kept at least how far from the excavation area?
D: 5 m
Reference: Cl. 5.4 n): heavy equipment, material or excavating machinery shall be kept clear from the excavation area by at least 3 m.

Question: Which barricading arrangement around an open trench meets KOC.SA.026?
A: Barrier tape tied between steel rebars
B: Hard fixed barriers with reflective warning signs
C: Rope strung between rebars at each corner
D: Spoil heaped along the edge as a bund
Reference: Cl. 4.3 / 5.4 k): hard fixed barriers with reflective warning notices, signs and flashing lights; tapes and rebars shall not be used as barriers.

Question: An excavation in Type B soil will exceed 1 m in depth. Which shoring arrangement meets KOC.SA.026?
A: No shoring if the sides are sloped at 30°
B: Sheeting 450 mm above ground; boards ≤ 750 mm apart
C: Polling boards 2 m apart; braces 2 m apart
D: No shoring if the trench is under 2 m deep
Reference: Cl. 5.6.1.2 a): Type B over 1 m — shoring required; sheeting at least 450 mm above ground; polling boards ≤ 750 mm apart; horizontal braces ≤ 1 m apart.

Question: In addition to the Excavation Notification, which work permit is required for excavation using a mechanical excavator?
D: Vehicle Entry Permit only
Reference: Cl. 5.3 e) / 5.6.2: a Hot Work Permit is required for excavation involving a mechanical excavator; a Cold Work Permit for manual excavation.

Question: How does KOC.SA.027 define 'High Voltage'?
C: A system voltage of 1000 V and above
D: A system voltage of 3300 V and above
Reference: Cl. 2.0: High Voltage – a system voltage of 3300 volts and above; Low Voltage – not exceeding 440 volts.

Question: Portable tools and extension cords above 50 V to ground that are frequently plugged and unplugged must be protected by an RCD with a maximum trip setting of:
D: 300 mA
Reference: Cl. 5.1: such equipment must be protected by permanent or portable RCDs with a 30 mA maximum current setting.

Question: A crane must pass under an existing 132 kV overhead power line. What is the minimum vertical clearance required between the lowest conductor and the top of the equipment?
Reference: Cl. 5.1 table: for 33 kV & 132 kV lines, minimum vertical safety clearance from lowest conductor to top of equipment is 5 m (10 m from ground).

Question: A portable hand lamp on a trailing lead is needed inside a confined space. What does KOC.SA.027 require?
A: Supply not exceeding 24 V and explosion-proof type
B: Supply not exceeding 110 V with an RCD
C: Supply not exceeding 240 V with double insulation
D: Any lamp, if the space is gas free
Reference: Cl. 5.2: for a portable hand lamp on a trailing lead inside a confined space, supply voltage shall not exceed 24 V and only explosion-proof type shall be used.

Question: When an isolated LV/HV conductor is earthed by installing a copper earthing conductor, what is its minimum cross-section?
D: 25 sq. mm
Reference: Cl. 5.3 C: each conductor shall be earthed by fixed earthing switch, CB, or a copper conductor of minimum cross section 25 sq. mm.

Question: Before starting work inside a substation protected by a CO2 or clean-agent suppression system, what must the authorized electrical person do?
A: Disable the fire alarm panel for the whole shift
B: Switch the system to Manual/Maintenance mode
C: Open all doors so any released gas can escape
D: Keep the system on Auto and wear an SCBA set
Reference: Cl. 4.4 / 5.3 A: turn the system to Manual/Maintenance mode on entry and return it to Normal (Auto) mode after the job and evacuation; record in the logbook.

Question: A worker is unconscious and still in contact with an electrical source. What does KOC.SA.027 say should be done first?
A: Pull the victim away by the clothing
B: Free the victim using a Rescue Stick
C: Pour water on the equipment to trip it
D: Wait for Maintenance before touching
Reference: Cl. 5.2: the victim should be removed safely from the electrical source by means of a Rescue Stick and artificial respiration given by trained personnel.

Question: Under the 'Test Before Touch' requirement of KOC.SA.027, how must the voltage tester itself be checked?
A: Only once a year when it is calibrated
B: On a known live source before and after use
C: Only before use, with its self-test button
D: Not needed when the tester is brand new
Reference: Cl. 5.1: Test Before Touch includes verifying test instruments on a known energized source before and after the test for absence of voltage.

Question: Before cutting an isolated high voltage cable, what must be done at the point of cut?
A: Wrap the cable with insulating tape
B: Spike it with a spiking gun or earthed spike
C: Test insulation resistance at 5 kV first
D: Hang a caution notice at the cut point
Reference: Cl. 5.3 D: HV cables shall be spiked at the point where they are to be cut by a spiking gun or a wooden-shafted, earthed steel-shod spike.

Question: A single crane will lift a load equal to 80% of its rated capacity at the planned radius. Under KOC.SA.029, this lift is:
A: A standard lift, since it is below 100% of capacity
B: A critical lift, because it exceeds 75% of rated capacity
C: A critical lift only if it also exceeds 50 tonnes
D: A standard lift if it is done in daylight
Reference: Cl. 2.0 Critical lift: loads exceeding 75% of the rated capacity of any one crane.

Question: Which of the following lifts is classified as a critical lift by height under KOC.SA.029?
A: A lift exceeding 10 m in height
B: A lift exceeding 20 m in height
C: A lift exceeding 30 m in height
D: A lift exceeding 50 m in height
Reference: Cl. 2.0 Critical lift: lifts which exceed 30 m in height (also > 50 tonnes, > 75% capacity, multiple cranes, man-lifting, etc.).

Question: What is the minimum age for an operator of load handling equipment under KOC.SA.029?
D: 25 years
Reference: Cl. 2.0 Operator: should be minimum 21 years of age, with 3rd party training certificates for the equipment.

Question: A lifting sling is inspected in November. According to the KOC.SA.029 quarterly colour code, which colour should it carry?
D: White
Reference: Cl. 5.2: Q1 Apr–Jun Green; Q2 Jul–Sep Yellow; Q3 Oct–Dec Blue; Q4 Jan–Mar White.

Question: Above what wind speed at the personnel platform must a man-lifting operation not begin, or be terminated if in progress?
D: 72 km/h
Reference: Cl. 5.6.5: when wind speed exceeds 15 mph (24 km/h) at the personnel platform, man-lifting must not begin or must be terminated.

Question: What minimum size of outrigger pad does KOC.SA.029 recommend under each crane outrigger float?
A: Same size as the outrigger foot
B: At least twice the size of the outrigger foot
C: At least three times the size of the outrigger foot
D: At least five times the size of the outrigger foot
Reference: Cl. 5.6.3: outrigger pad size should be at least three times the size of the outrigger foot.

Question: When must a wire rope be removed from service due to broken wires under KOC.SA.029?
A: When any single broken wire is found
B: When broken wires exceed 10% in 8 diameters
C: When broken wires exceed 25% in one lay
D: Only when a full strand is broken
Reference: Cl. 5.8.3: wire rope shall not be used if, in any length of eight diameters, total visible broken wires exceed 10% of total wires.

Question: What is the maximum speed at which material handling equipment (e.g. a forklift) may be driven while operating inside a company facility?
D: 20 km/h
Reference: Cl. 5.8.4: the equipment shall not be driven at a speed exceeding 8 km per hour while operating in a company facility.

Question: A contractor installs a fixed tower crane at a KOC site. What is the maximum validity of the Controlling Team's approval before the approval process must be repeated?
D: 24 months
Reference: Cl. 5.3: approval for contractor fixed / permanently installed load handling equipment shall not exceed 12 months.

Question: Unless conditions warrant greater clearance, painting should not be carried out within what distance of potential ignition sources such as welding or flame cutting?
D: 100 feet
Reference: Cl. 5.10: no painting should be carried out within 75 feet of potential ignition sources.

Question: Which surface preparation method is prohibited under KOC.SA.030?
D: Power tool cleaning
Reference: Cl. 5.4: sand blasting is prohibited.

Question: Which of the following must NOT be used for solvent cleaning of surfaces before painting?
B: Alkali cleaners from an approved supplier
D: Water-based degreasers
Reference: Cl. 5.4: benzene, gasoline, carbon tetrachloride and chlorinated hydrocarbons with low TLVs (< 20 ppm) shall not be used for solvent cleaning.

Question: If practical alternatives exist, solvents and paints shall not be applied to surfaces warmer than:
Reference: Cl. 5.10: solvents and paints shall not be applied to surfaces warmer than 80°C if practical alternatives exist (and not flushed into containers hotter than 50°C).

Question: A painter suffers a small skin puncture from high-pressure fluid from an airless spray gun. What does KOC.SA.030 require?
A: Clean with solvent and apply a plaster
B: Continue work and report at the end of shift
D: Wash with soap and monitor for 24 hours
Reference: Cl. 5.5: emergency medical care shall be obtained immediately if any high pressure fluid penetrates the skin; injection injuries can be extremely serious.

Question: Inside a confined space, during which activities must all personnel wear respirable air-fed hoods under KOC.SA.030?
A: Only during abrasive blasting of surfaces
B: Only during airless spray painting work
C: During blasting, spraying, solvent or brush work
D: Only when the LEL reading exceeds 10%
Reference: Cl. 5.8: air-fed hoods shall be worn inside confined spaces whenever blasting or spray painting, solvent cleaning or brush painting is in progress.

Question: Where should paint or thinner be decanted from one container to another?
A: Inside the store, near the shelves
B: In the open air, away from hazardous operations
C: Inside the spray booth, exhaust running
D: At the work face, beside the item painted
Reference: Cl. 5.11: dispensing or decanting shall not take place within the store but in the open air away from areas of hazardous operations.

Question: What must be done whenever an airless spray gun is left unattended?
C: Point the gun into the paint bucket
D: Disconnect the earthing lead
Reference: Cl. 5.5: the trigger safety catch shall be engaged whenever the airless gun is left unattended; tip guard always in place while spraying.

Question: Under KOC.SA.031, an activity is defined as 'work at height' when it is carried out at an elevated location higher than:
Reference: Cl. 2.0: work at height is an activity at an elevated location of more than 1.8 m (6 ft) from the working ground level.

Question: What minimum load must a fixed anchor point be capable of supporting for each person attached to it?
Reference: Cl. 2.0 / 5.2.3.3: an anchorage must be capable of supporting at least 5,000 lb (22.2 kN) for each person attached.

Question: Which lanyard specification complies with KOC.SA.031 for use with a full body harness?
A: Max 1.8 m, shock absorber, self-locking hooks
C: Max 3 m, made of polypropylene rope
D: Any length, shortened by tying knots
Reference: Cl. 5.2.3.2: maximum lanyard length 1.8 m (6 ft), self-locking hooks each end, shock absorber; never shortened with knots; no polypropylene.

Question: As a general guideline, at what length of climb on a fixed ladder must appropriate fall protection be provided?
D: 9 m (30 ft) or more
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2: appropriate fall protection must be provided whenever the length of climb on a fixed ladder equals or exceeds 24 ft (7.3 m).

Question: Which guardrail arrangement meets the KOC.SA.031 edge protection requirements?
A: Top rail 750 mm high; no mid rail needed
B: Top rail ≥ 950 mm; no gap over 470 mm
C: Top rail 1,200 mm; gaps up to 600 mm
D: Steel banding as top rail at 1,000 mm
Reference: Cl. 5.2.1 / 5.2.3.8: main guard rail at least 950 mm (normally 1,000 mm); no gap more than 470 mm; steel/plastic banding not permitted as rails.

Question: Which statement about personal fall arrest equipment is correct under KOC.SA.031?
A: A body belt may be used if it has a shock absorber
B: Body belts are prohibited; harness with 100% tie-off
C: 100% tie-off is needed only above 6 m in height
D: One lanyard is enough when moving between anchors
Reference: Cl. 5.2.3.1: full body harness with two shock-absorbing lanyards; use of a body belt for fall arrest is prohibited; ensure 100% tie-off.

Question: In addition to the user's visual pre-use check, how often must the Controlling Team ensure harnesses, lanyards and lifelines are formally inspected and tagged?
D: Annually
Reference: Cl. 5.3: all fall-arresting equipment shall be subjected to a monthly inspection program and tagged if fit for use.

Question: A worker's lanyard arrested a short fall, and the shock absorber appears undamaged. What does KOC.SA.031 require?
A: Re-use it after a careful visual check
B: Re-use it after re-packing the absorber
D: Use it for work restraint only
Reference: Cl. 5.2.3.2 / 5.3: components subjected to impact loading shall be removed from service; equipment involved in a fall must not be used again.

Question: Use of a crane-suspended man basket to lift workers is permitted only in exceptional cases. How must the lift be classified and planned?
A: As a standard lift with a JSA only
B: As a critical lift with a Critical Lift Plan
C: As routine work not requiring a permit
D: As a standard lift if fitted with guardrails
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2: use of a man basket shall be considered a critical lift; a Critical Lift Plan shall be prepared per KOC.SA.029.

Question: In a cylinder store, oxygen cylinders must be separated from fuel-gas cylinders by a minimum of:
A: 3 m, or a 1 m high barrier
B: 6.1 m, or a 1.5 m high fire-rated barrier
C: 10 m, with no barrier option allowed
D: 15 m, or any solid wall of any height
Reference: Cl. 5.4: oxygen separated from fuel-gas cylinders by at least 20 ft (6.1 m) or a non-combustible barrier at least 5 ft (1.5 m) high, ½-hour fire resistance.

Question: According to the hose colour coding in KOC.SA.035 (BS EN ISO 3821), which colour hose is used for acetylene?
D: Black
Reference: Cl. 5.7: Blue – Oxygen; Red – Acetylene; Orange – Propane, LPG, Natural Gas or Fuel Gas.

Question: Compressed gas cylinders must not be exposed to temperatures (including direct sunlight) exceeding:
Reference: Cl. 5.4: any cylinder containing compressed gas shall not be subjected to a temperature exceeding 54.5°C (130°F).

Question: Why must acetylene cylinders be stored, handled and used in the vertical position?
A: To let the porous mass settle evenly
B: To stop liquid acetone escaping to the valve
C: To keep the cylinder cooler in sunlight
D: To make the colour code easier to read
Reference: Cl. 5.1: acetylene is dissolved in acetone; cylinders must be kept vertical to prevent liquid acetone escaping and damaging valves and equipment.

Question: As a means of distinguishing gases, which valve outlet thread is used on acetylene, hydrogen and other flammable gas cylinders?
D: The same thread as oxygen
Reference: Cl. 5.2: right-hand thread for oxygen and non-flammable gases; left-hand thread for acetylene, hydrogen and flammable gases.

Question: A flashback occurs during oxy-acetylene cutting, but the hose looks intact from outside. What must be done with the hose?
A: Purge it with oxygen and continue the job
B: Leak test with soapy water and re-use if OK
C: Discard it immediately; the inner wall is damaged
D: Cut off the last metre and re-use the rest
Reference: Cl. 5.7: any hose in which a flashback has occurred will have its inner wall damaged and must be discarded immediately.

Question: After opening a gas cylinder valve fully for use, how should it be left?
A: Fully open against the back stop
B: A half turn back from full open
D: Fully open and taped in position
Reference: Cl. 5.5: an open valve shall be left a half turn back from full open so that movement to the back stop indicates the valve is open.

Question: 'Snifting' (briefly opening a cylinder valve to clear dirt before fitting a regulator) is permitted for most gases. For which gas is it NEVER allowed?
D: Hydrogen
Reference: Cl. 5.5: hydrogen shall never be snifted as it may ignite spontaneously.

Question: According to KOC.HE.003, what is the permissible flammable gas limit for authorized cold work?
D: Below 25% LEL
Reference: Cl. 5.6.1: the permissible limit for authorized cold work is below 10% of the LEL (hot work: 0% LEL).

Question: Where periodic gas testing is used during hot or cold work, the test interval must not exceed:
D: 4 hours
Reference: Cl. 5.6.1 / 5.6.3: testing continuously or periodically with the test interval not exceeding two hours.

Question: When gas testing for hot work, the gas test area shall include everywhere within what distance of the hot work location?
Reference: Cl. 5.7: the gas test area shall include everywhere within 50 ft (15 m) of the hot work location.

Question: A confined space is being mechanically ventilated by an exhaust fan. When should the gas test be carried out?
A: While the fan is running at full speed
B: Immediately after switching the fan off
C: About 10 minutes after stopping the exhaust fan
D: Only after the fan has been removed from the manway
Reference: Cl. 5.7: for a mechanically ventilated confined space, test only after 10 minutes of stopping the exhaust fan to avoid the effect of air draft.

Question: Which acceptable exposure levels (TLV-TWA) does KOC.HE.003 state for carbon monoxide and sulphur dioxide?
D: CO 35 ppm; SO2 1 ppm
Reference: Cl. 5.3: acceptable levels — carbon monoxide 25 ppm (TLV-TWA, ACGIH) and sulphur dioxide 5 ppm (TLV-TWA, KEPA).

Question: Under the TLV-STEL definition in KOC.HE.003, exposures above the TLV-TWA up to the STEL should be:
A: Less than 15 minutes each, no more than 4 times a day, at least 60 minutes apart
B: Less than 30 minutes each, no more than 2 times a day, at least 30 minutes apart
C: Less than 15 minutes each, unlimited times a day
D: Less than 60 minutes each, once a day
Reference: Cl. 2.0: exposures above TWA up to STEL should be < 15 minutes, no more than four times per day, with at least 60 minutes between them.

Question: Which type of portable gas detector must be used for all INITIAL gas tests under KOC.HE.003?
B: Aspirated monitor with built-in sampling pump
C: Single-gas H2S badge clipped on the collar
D: Fixed area gas detector at the facility
Reference: Cl. 5.4.1: aspirated gas monitors (built-in pump) — all initial gas tests shall be done with this type of detector.

Question: When testing a vessel where H2S could be present, where is it essential to sample?
A: As close to the top of the vessel as possible
B: Only at the manway opening of the vessel
C: As close to the bottom of the vessel as possible
D: Only through the vessel's vent line
Reference: Cl. 5.5 / 5.7: H2S is heavier than air (1.19); sample as close to the bottom as possible.

Question: A gas detector is taken from an air-conditioned office to a hot outdoor worksite. What does KOC.HE.003 advise before using it?
A: Use it immediately, as sensors are temperature compensated
B: Allow 5–30 minutes for the instrument to stabilize to the temperature
C: Re-calibrate it in the field with test gas every time
D: Keep it in a plastic bag to avoid condensation during the test
Reference: Cl. 5.1: allow sufficient time for the equipment to temperature stabilize prior to use, which may vary between 5–30 minutes.

Question: A contractor has 120 workers at a site. Under KOC.HE.004, what is the minimum number of first aiders required?
Reference: Cl. 5.4.1 c): one first aider per every 50 employees / contract workers (minimum one). 120 workers → 3 first aiders.

Question: What is the required provision of first aid kits under KOC.HE.004?
D: One kit per facility, regardless of numbers
Reference: Cl. 5.5 / 5.8: one first aid kit shall be made available for every 50 workers.

Question: To remain appropriately qualified, how often must a KOC first aider attend a first aid refresher course?
D: Every 5 years
Reference: Cl. 5.5 B: first aiders attend refresher training courses every three (3) years.

Question: How often must designated first aiders attend a CPR and AED training session?
D: Every 3 years
Reference: Cl. 5.5 B / 5.6.1: attend CPR & AED training session once every year.

Question: Under KOC.HE.004 and Kuwait labour requirements, a contractor must establish a First Aid Room wherever how many workers are engaged?
D: 100 or more
Reference: Cl. 5.4.1 a) / 5.5 II A: a First Aid Room shall be established wherever fifty (50) or more workers are engaged.

Question: Which statement about first aid kit containers is correct under KOC.HE.004?
A: Locked, to prevent theft of contents
B: Clearly labelled, visible and not locked
C: Opened only by the site medic
D: Kept inside the supervisor's office
Reference: Cl. 5.8.1: the first aid container should be prominently displayed, labelled 'First Aid Box', accessible, and should not be locked.

Question: Within what time must a first aid case be reported in MyHSSE under KOC.HE.004 (with KOC.GE.007)?
D: Within 7 days
Reference: Cl. 4: report in MyHSSE within 24 hours of incident occurrence (as per KOC.GE.007 & KOC.HE.020).

Question: Which statement best describes the role of a first aider under KOC.HE.004?
A: Give initial care within training; refer to medical advice
B: Provide ongoing treatment until full recovery
C: Prescribe medicines from the first aid kit stock
D: Decide whether the injury needs to be reported
Reference: Cl. 5.6: first aiders undertake initial treatment consistent with training; when in doubt recommend medical advice; not responsible for ongoing care.

Question: In an open yard storage area, what is the maximum height to which combustible materials may be piled?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.1: combustible materials shall in no case be piled higher than 20 ft (6.1 m).

Question: What minimum width must driveways between and around combustible storage piles be kept?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.1: driveways between and around combustible storage piles must be at least 15 ft (4.57 m) wide.

Question: Under KOC.GE.034, combustible material may NOT be stored outdoors within what distance of a building or structure?
Reference: Cl. 5.2.1: no combustible material may be stored outdoors within 10 ft (3.048 m) of a building or structure.

Question: In an indoor store with sprinklers, what minimum clearance must be kept between the top of stored material and the sprinkler deflectors?
D: 48 inches (1.2 m)
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2: clearance of at least 36 inches (0.9144 m) must be maintained between stored material and sprinkler deflectors.

Question: Non-compatible materials that may create a fire, explosion or reaction hazard must be segregated in storage by a barrier with a fire resistance of at least:
D: 2 hours
Reference: Cl. 5.2.2: non-compatible materials must be segregated by a barrier having a fire resistance of at least 1 hour.

Question: Where needed for access to doors, windows or standpipe connections, aisles must be kept at least how wide?
Reference: Cl. 5.3: keep aisles at least 3 ft (0.9144 m) wide where necessary for access to doors, windows or standpipe connections.

Question: What does KOC.GE.034 recommend regarding end-of-day cleaning on construction sites?
A: Cleaning is done by a separate night crew only
B: Work stops half an hour early for site cleaning
C: Housekeeping is done once a week on rest day
D: Cleaning is needed only before HSE inspections
Reference: Cl. 5.0 Note: it is highly recommended that construction activities cease half an hour before and that time be used for area cleaning / housekeeping.

Question: Under KOC.GE.034, what must Team Leaders ensure regarding gasoline within the battery limits of KOC projects, facilities and drilling sites?
A: Gasoline may be stored in approved jerry cans up to 20 litres
B: No gasoline storage or refuelling is allowed
C: Gasoline may be stored if kept 15 m from buildings
D: Gasoline refuelling is allowed only during daylight
Reference: Cl. 4.1: ensure that no gasoline storage or its refuelling is allowed in the KOC jurisdiction battery limit of any projects / facilities / drilling sites.

Question: A worker's personal H2S monitor goes into alarm near a sour wellhead. What is the correct immediate response under KOC.GE.036?
A: Run downwind to the nearest vehicle and drive off
B: Don escape set, check windsock, walk crosswind
C: Stay in place and wait for Control Room instructions
D: Help colleagues nearer the release before leaving
Reference: Cl. 5.x Escape from H2S Release: put on escape-only respirator, observe windsock, walk (don't run) crosswind to Control Room / muster point; do not attempt to rescue others.

Question: When purchasing personal H2S monitors, KOC.GE.036 recommends two alarm set points. What are they?
A: First alarm at or below 5 ppm; second at or below 10 ppm
B: First alarm at or below 10 ppm; second at or below 15 ppm
C: First alarm at or below 15 ppm; second at or below 50 ppm
D: First alarm at or below 20 ppm; second at or below 100 ppm
Reference: Cl. 5.3 c): units should alarm at or below 10 ppm (TWA/8 hrs) for the first alarm and at or below 15 ppm (STEL/15 min) for the second.

Question: According to KOC.GE.036 Table 2, when H2S is between 10 and 15 ppm, work without respiratory protection is permitted for:
B: 15 min, up to 4 times per shift
C: 30 min, up to 2 times per shift
D: Not permitted at all
Reference: Table 2: between 10 to 15 ppm, work is permitted for a 15-minute period without RPE, up to 4 times during an 8-hour shift.

Question: Gas testing shows 60 ppm H2S at a worksite and the source cannot be isolated, purged or ventilated. Under KOC.GE.036, what is required for work to proceed?
D: No work is allowed above 50 ppm
Reference: Table 2: up to 100 ppm, work is permitted with positive-pressure supplied air respirator or 30-min SCBA only if the source cannot be isolated; above 100 ppm entry only for rescue.

Question: Where should a personal H2S monitor be worn?
A: Inside the coverall pocket, away from dust
B: On the belt at waist level
D: Clipped to the safety boot
Reference: Cl. 5.3 c): worn outside clothing close to the head, as this is where H2S will be ingested; shoulder or breast pocket is optimal.

Question: A crew of 14 workers will carry out maintenance in an area where H2S hazards may be present, but the facility itself is not sour. What gas detection does KOC.GE.036 require?
A: One personal gas monitor for the crew
C: No detector, as the facility is not sour
D: One personal monitor per five workers
Reference: Cl. 4 Field Workers c): one personal monitor per crew below 10 workers; more than 10 workers — a tripod-mounted portable multi-gas detector; sour facility — every worker carries one.

Question: KOC.GE.036 defines 'sour' hydrocarbons as oil or gas containing H2S above:
Reference: Cl. 2.0: sour hydrocarbons contain more than 0.001%, i.e. 10 ppm of hydrogen sulphide.

Question: Why can opening a vessel that handled sour product be hazardous even after it has been drained?
A: Dry pyrophoric iron sulphide can self-ignite in air
B: H2S turns lighter than air once the vessel is open
C: Rust deposits stop portable gas detectors working
D: Sulphur dioxide is released when water is added
Reference: Cl. 5.2 f): pyrophoric scale (ferrous sulphide) reacts exothermically with oxygen and, when dry, auto-ignites at ambient temperature.

Question: How often must personnel who may enter H2S hazardous areas receive H2S awareness training under KOC.GE.036?
D: Every 3 years
Reference: Cl. 5.4 a): personnel who may be required to enter H2S hazardous areas shall receive annual H2S awareness.

Question: What is the minimum isolation standard required for entry into a vessel or confined space under KOC.PS.016?
A: Single block valve, locked and tagged
B: Double block and bleed valve isolation
D: ESD valve closed with actuator enabled
Reference: Cl. 5.1 / 5.5.1: the minimum isolation standard for vessel or confined space entry is positive isolation; it is mandatory for such entry.

Question: Which is the PREFERRED method of achieving positive isolation according to KOC.PS.016?
A: Closing two block valves with an open bleed
B: Spool removal with rated blank flanges on the live ends
C: Inserting a spade only when spool removal is easier
D: Closing a single gate valve and locking it
Reference: Cl. 5.5.1: spool removal is the preferred method of positive isolation; spade insertion where spool removal is not reasonably practicable; valves alone are not positive isolation.

Question: Before breaking containment, how long does KOC.PS.016 recommend that isolation integrity tests be conducted, as a minimum?
D: 30 minutes
Reference: Cl. 5.7: all isolations shall be tested and shown to be effective before containment is broken; integrity tests recommended for a minimum of 10 minutes.

Question: What is the minimum recommended frequency for monitoring the integrity of isolation points while containment is broken?
A: Once per week, at the start of the work week
B: Once per day, at the start of day shift only
C: Once per shift and just before breaking containment
D: Only when the Work Party requests a check
Reference: Cl. 5.8: minimum recommended monitoring frequency is once per shift and immediately prior to breaking containment; results recorded at shift handover.

Question: Which type of valve shall NOT be used as a form of isolation under KOC.PS.016?
D: Fail-closed ESD valve with actuator disabled
Reference: Cl. 5.9: non-return (check) valves, flow control valves and pressure relief valves shall not be used as a form of isolation.

Question: During work under a double block and bleed isolation, the gauge on the bleed between the two block valves starts to show pressure. What must happen?
A: Open the bleed fully and continue working
B: Stop work and review and amend the isolation
C: Tighten the upstream valve and continue
D: Record it at shift handover and continue
Reference: Cl. 5.5.2: the void between block valves must remain at 0 barg; if pressure increases, work shall stop and the isolation be reviewed and amended.

Question: Besides vessel entry, KOC.PS.016 recommends positive isolation for long-duration isolations. What duration is given as an example?
D: More than one month
Reference: Cl. 5.5.1: positive isolation recommended for long duration isolations, e.g. more than one week, hot work, and new/out-of-service equipment interfaces.

Question: Under KOC.PS.016, how are bleeds and vents that form part of an isolation to be controlled?
A: Padlocked shut like the block valves
B: Left untagged so they can be operated
C: Tagged and recorded, without a lock
D: Removed from the line and blanked
Reference: Cl. 5.13: bleeds and vents do not require a securing device, as their position may change, but they require a bleed/vent tag and must be documented on the Certificate.
